mcts._num_simulations_note: 1200, not 600: at 140 actions 600 sims is ~4.3 visits per action, so the visit histogram barely differs from the prior it was seeded with and the policy target reinforces it. Self-play is 93% of the iteration, so this ~2x's wall clock.

training._iters_note: num_iterations/games_per_iteration are per variant; N=4 games run ~3x longer so it buys fewer of them for the same wall clock
training._replay_buffer_note: 100k ~= 7 iterations of coverage at N=2 — the regime runs/n2_5x5_buf10k_v1 validated.
training._ply_counted_note: max_game_moves and explore_moves both count plies, not rounds — set per variant so each player gets the same budget; see variants.n2/n4
training._discount_unit_note: Per-variant: 'round' decays per the mover's own turns, 'ply' per move by anybody. Measured better at N=2, worse at N=4.
training._accept_margin_note: 0.08 at eval_games=160: SE is 0.040, so the 0.58 bar is +2.0 sigma (~2% false accepts). The old 0.05 at 80 games was +0.9 sigma = 19%, and v4's post-iter-15 accepts were consistent with pure noise.
training._wall_mask_note: Race-only self-play for the opening iterations. Walls are 128 of 140 actions at 9x9 (32 of 44 at 5x5), so an untrained policy walls ~91% of the time and never learns the race. Eval always plays the full game. 0 = off.

parallel._num_workers_note: Match the pod's cgroup cpu quota (16). Above it the jupyter server stops answering its own health check, whose entrypoint runs pkill -9 on failure.
